forest_03_001.speaker: narrator
forest_03_001.text: The measuring assistant arrived with a wooden case longer than his arm and a breakfast bun held between his teeth. Pei Yun took the case while he freed his hands. Inside lay folded rods, brass pins, a waxed cord, and a plumb weight wrapped like an infant. Wen asked which object was most likely to kill them if dropped. The assistant pointed to his unpaid breakfast. Pei returned the case and told him to finish eating before they left.

forest_03_002.speaker: pei_yun
forest_03_002.text: The old survey begins at the lower bridge pier, not at the stone everyone now calls the beginning. That stone acquired its name after the bridge was rebuilt. I know this because I carried lunches during the rebuilding and was sent away whenever I asked questions. You can learn a surprising amount while being sent away. It does not make every remembered lunch into a measurement. We will start at the pier whose footing survived.

forest_03_003.speaker: narrator
forest_03_003.text: At the bridge, the river had shrunk to a narrow dark vein beneath a sheet of broken ice. The surviving pier was half buried in gravel. The assistant swept its face with a brush and found the old cut mark at the height shown in Pei's survey. Its corner had chipped, but the central stroke remained. He recorded both. Lin held the cord above the water while Wen stood on the bank, looking uncomfortable with being useful so slowly.

forest_03_004.speaker: wen_cai
forest_03_004.text: When I cut wood, I can point to a stump at the end of the day and say that is what happened. Today we have brushed a stone, argued about a scratch, and written down the argument. I know why it matters. I am also freezing. If the old surveyor was half as cold, perhaps his mysterious abbreviations mean 'get on with it.' Pei Yun, please tell me at least one of them means that.

forest_03_005.speaker: pei_yun
forest_03_005.text: This one means 'reed bed beyond the bend.' I am afraid your proposed translation would move the boundary into the river. This one means 'winter path retained.' This one is my father's mark beside the measurement, because he witnessed the placement. I used to think the mark was a bird. He was disappointed when I told him. He had spent years teaching himself to make his name look respectable, and his daughter saw a chicken.

forest_03_006.speaker: narrator
forest_03_006.text: The first line crossed a low meadow. Frost turned each blade of grass into a little pale spear. The assistant set intermediate pins, read the slope, and asked Lin to move her end of the cord twice. Nobody could pull a valley straight by pulling hard. When Wen tried, the cord lifted off one support and changed the reading. The assistant explained without scolding. Wen looked relieved, then embarrassed to have been relieved.

forest_03_007.speaker: narrator
forest_03_007.text: At the far edge, they found the base of an old marker embedded in a tangle of roots. Its top had broken away. A newer stone stood seven paces uphill, broad and clean under the snow. Shi Lan inspected the ground around both without touching either. The newer stone's footing was shallow and packed with pale chips. That did not tell them who had placed it or why. It did tell them the two stones could not simply be treated as the same object.

forest_03_008.speaker: shi_lan
forest_03_008.text: Keep the walking route open until we have looked at the whole line. I want the cutters told there are two placements under review, not that one has been condemned. If we announce a theft before we know whether the broken stone was moved after a flood, somebody will remember exactly the accusation he heard and forget every qualification around it. The fresh chips are useful. An angry story built from them would be less useful.

forest_03_009.speaker: narrator
forest_03_009.text: Pei knelt beside the broken base longer than the others. A root had grown through the old setting, pushing one side outward. She placed her palm on the root, then took it away before the assistant began drawing. Lin noticed a crease of white skin across her thumb. For a moment she looked younger and much angrier. Wen asked whether she had known it was broken. She said she had known it had become hard to find.

forest_03_010.speaker: lin_yue
forest_03_010.text: That is an answer to where it was, not to what you knew about its condition. You do not have to give me the other answer here, with everybody cold and waiting. But the assistant will need it before he compares the placements. If there is a reason you do not want the newer stone questioned, tell him that reason too. We cannot measure around a worry that only one of us knows is there.

forest_03_011.speaker: narrator
forest_03_011.text: Pei gave her a look sharp enough to make Wen suddenly interested in his boot. Then she told the assistant that a winter flood had damaged the lower marker eleven years earlier, and a road crew had set the higher stone the following spring. She had seen the work but not the order. Her father's old line and the newer road line might have been intended to serve different purposes. She had allowed neighbors to use the newer one as if the distinction did not matter.

forest_03_012.speaker: pei_yun
forest_03_012.text: When people ask which stone to follow on a snowy night, you point to the stone they can see. You do not make them stand in the wind while you explain eleven years of paperwork. Then spring comes and everyone is busy. Then another winter comes. I have had time to repair this confusion. That is the part you are waiting for me to say. There. I have said it, and the stone is still broken.

forest_03_013.speaker: narrator
forest_03_013.text: They ate beside a fallen trunk. The trunk's bark held so many small holes that it resembled a sieve. Shi Lan tapped one with a knife handle and explained which insects had hollowed it before the storm brought it down. Wen asked whether the forest ever suffered an injury for a single clear reason. The warden said that it probably did, but foresters generally arrived after three other things had made the first reason difficult to see.

forest_03_014.speaker: narrator
forest_03_014.text: Lin shared her dried beans with the assistant, whose bun had been less substantial than it looked. Pei accepted bread from Wen and did not thank him until her second bite. He acted as though he had not noticed the delay. Across the meadow, the new marker cast a short blue shadow. Lin tried to imagine the road crew setting it eleven years ago: tired men, a practical decision, and nobody expecting the decision to become a debt.

forest_03_015.speaker: narrator
forest_03_015.text: Beyond the meadow, the cord line reached a gully that the old survey described as dry. Water now trickled beneath a crust of snow. The assistant measured its width at the documented crossing and made a separate sketch of the present channel. A landslip had stripped soil from the upper bank. They could see old roots hanging in the air. Shi Lan sent Wen ahead along the safe side to check whether the cutting track approached the unstable edge.

forest_03_016.speaker: wen_cai
forest_03_016.text: The track comes down above it. There are fresh wheel ruts, but they turn before the lip. I found a sack tie caught on a thorn and left it there. I also found where someone dragged a log sideways. We do that when a cart cannot take the bend. Those marks alone would not tell you whether the load was legal. They would tell you a man with more enthusiasm than judgment tried to steer on ice.

forest_03_017.speaker: narrator
forest_03_017.text: The assistant marked the ruts as recent surface features and kept them off the boundary calculation. This disappointed Lin more than she expected. Fresh tracks seemed to promise a quick answer, the sort of answer that made an afternoon's work feel important. The older measurements promised only more walking. She folded the disappointment into her pocket with her empty bread cloth and followed the cord. The forest did not rearrange itself to reward their preferred kind of clue.

forest_03_018.speaker: narrator
forest_03_018.text: At the second marker, they found two iron holes in the rock face where a notice frame had once stood. No frame remained. Pei's survey showed a turning point there and a separate dotted line for temporary winter passage. Shi Lan paced the passage downhill. It led toward the broken cabbage fence, then into the cold hollow. The route was narrow enough that a large animal and a laden person would have little room to pass each other.

forest_03_019.speaker: shi_lan
forest_03_019.text: This is why I want the old passage examined before anyone builds a new fence across it. I am not promising that every dotted line drawn thirty-seven years ago remains suitable. The ground has changed, and so have the houses. But the animal did not invent this low crossing yesterday. If we close the safer bend and leave only this throat, we will keep meeting it at the worst possible angle.

forest_03_020.speaker: narrator
forest_03_020.text: A wind came up while they were taking the final reading. Powdered snow drifted from the branches and filled the assistant's collar. Wen laughed until a second gust found his own neck. Pei packed the old survey before its edges grew damp. They had enough light to return by the lower path, not enough to inspect the high cutting stand as well. Shi Lan chose the return. Nobody pretended that ending a day's work was surrendering the whole inquiry.

forest_03_021.speaker: narrator
forest_03_021.text: At the gate, the clerk had posted the gathering rule in large letters and read it aloud to the first arriving families. The woman with the twig bundle stood nearby, testing the words against what she had been told yesterday. She asked about a fallen branch too heavy to carry alone. The clerk checked the rule before answering. Pei looked at him, then at her own rolled survey. Small corrections could be made before they aged into history.

forest_03_022.speaker: narrator
forest_03_022.text: In the office, the assistant laid the day's sketch beside the old survey and the current cutting licence. Three documents made three different shapes of the same hillside. The survey included the seasonal passage. The licence followed the higher road marker for one segment but cited no amended land boundary. The new shape left a wedge of timber apparently available to the northern crew. It also narrowed the path beside the cabbage pits. Nobody had to intend both effects for both to occur.

forest_03_023.speaker: pei_yun
forest_03_023.text: The road clerk may have copied the convenient line because everyone called it the boundary. My own silence helped make it convenient. That does not prove he invented it. I want the road order and the licence application compared before you decide who benefited on purpose. I will answer for what I saw. I will not manufacture a villain to make my answer seem less foolish.

forest_03_024.speaker: narrator
forest_03_024.text: Rong Sui came with a clean copy of the licence application. He had purchased the proposed northern output under a condition that cutting permission be obtained. The foreman's advance agreement had then described northern work as a repayment option without repeating that condition. Rong said his office used standard forms. Shi Lan asked to see the instruction sent with the form. His expression changed only slightly, but Lin noticed it because everyone else was looking at the seal.

forest_03_025.speaker: rong_sui
forest_03_025.text: I have the clerk's covering letter. It tells him to secure a workable remedy before making the advance. It does not tell him to promise permission. I also discussed the northern stand with him before he came. That discussion was not written down. He may say I encouraged certainty. I remember encouraging speed. Those can sound alike when a young man believes his pay depends on bringing back a signed page.

forest_03_026.speaker: narrator
forest_03_026.text: Long Qian leaned back, looking almost pleased. Then the assistant asked for his grain-house application. It used the same higher marker and described the old passage as disused. Long's clerk had copied a council summary rather than walking the route. The summary bore Pei's office stamp. Pei stared at it. She had approved the summary's road description, she said, before its phrase about disuse was added. The original draft would have to be found.

forest_03_027.speaker: long_qian
forest_03_027.text: If my clerk copied the wrong statement, I will correct my application. I will not agree that this makes every east-town deposit superior to a valley kitchen. Rong has buyers who can delay a heating order. I have people cooking grain every day. That difference is relevant even if both our papers are imperfect. Let us find the original summary, certainly. Let us also stop behaving as though better handwriting will boil tomorrow's porridge.

forest_03_028.speaker: narrator
forest_03_028.text: The cook, who had entered to collect the office's empty kettle, stopped in the doorway. She asked whether anybody had actually counted how much fuel one grain-house meal required. Long said his manager had. She asked whether that count was before or after the stove doors were repaired. He did not know. Rong began to smile and lost the smile when she asked whether his customers' deposits specified charcoal only or any suitable dry heating fuel.

forest_03_029.speaker: narrator
forest_03_029.text: A pause followed, satisfying only to the cook. The commission could investigate the boundary without assuming every requested bag was indispensable. Shi Lan arranged separate checks: the keeper would verify present usable charcoal and licensed billets, the kitchens would measure ordinary fuel use, and both buyers would bring their actual customer terms. Lin would assist the physical survey and carry messages within her paid hours. The cook reclaimed the kettle. Nobody had answered her first question yet.

forest_03_030.speaker: narrator
forest_03_030.text: After the meeting, Pei searched three drawers for the stamped draft. She knew the drawers so well that her hands moved before she looked. That familiarity made the failure more troubling. Lin offered to read the bundle on the floor. Pei nodded. The pages contained pig licences, bridge repairs, a complaint about an aggressive goose, and a receipt for lamp oil. The goose had received a clearer description than the winter passage.

forest_03_031.speaker: pei_yun
forest_03_031.text: It chased the tax assistant into the ditch. He came here wet, demanding immediate action against its owner. I asked whether he had entered the yard. He said that was not the point. I wrote down his answer because I thought the owner deserved to see it. There are days when I remember that goose with affection. Do not tell Shi Lan. She already thinks I become sentimental about the wrong residents.

forest_03_032.speaker: narrator
forest_03_032.text: They found the draft pinned behind a later bridge repair list. Its wording said the passage was little used during the preceding two mild winters. The circulated summary said it was disused. A clerk had shortened several phrases in the same way to fit one sheet. Pei had stamped the longer draft, not the printed summary. The difference could explain one misleading word. It could not establish whether anyone had deliberately relied on that word afterward.

forest_03_033.speaker: lin_yue
forest_03_033.text: We should ask the clerk how the short version was made and where it went. I want to call it careless because that would be easier than asking who welcomed the change. But I also want to call it deliberate because then I could be angry at one person. Neither wish tells us what happened. May I copy the two lines side by side for tomorrow, with the rest of the private notices still covered?

forest_03_034.speaker: narrator
forest_03_034.text: Pei allowed the paired copy. Then she sat down abruptly, pressing both palms against her knees. Her joints had endured the day's walking less quietly than her face suggested. Lin moved the footstool within reach and waited. Pei accepted it after a moment. Outside, the niece was singing to her paper Hart in a tune that changed whenever she forgot the next line. Pei listened, her mouth softening at each invented note.

forest_03_035.speaker: narrator
forest_03_035.text: That night Lin practiced two short sequences in the lodging courtyard. Frost made the packed earth treacherous. She lowered the tempo until each release and return was deliberate, stopping before fatigue pulled her shoulders upward. The fourth-stage traces remained what she had earned: two established arm pairs, imperfectly controlled when cold distracted her. Her frustration was familiar. So was the satisfaction of finishing without pretending that a difficult afternoon had made her stronger by itself.

forest_03_036.speaker: wen_cai
forest_03_036.text: I watched from the door because the cook told me not to interrupt. You look different when you practice. Not grander. Less eager to guess what the next person wants. I wondered whether cutting could be like that, if I had learned it before the foreman learned my name. Then you slipped on the frost, and I felt better. Sorry. I would have helped if you had fallen. It was still encouraging to see the wobble.

forest_03_037.speaker: narrator
forest_03_037.text: Lin threw him the cloth she had been using to dry her hands. He caught it, discovered it was icy, and protested. She asked whether he had learned anything from the foreman's private reply. The requested northern shift remained suspended; his licensed work turn would continue at the posted rate during the inquiry. His uncle had finally told the foreman that Wen had not made the promise. Wen said it as though describing weather he did not trust.

forest_03_038.speaker: narrator
forest_03_038.text: On the tenth morning, the former road crew leader arrived from a lower settlement. He was carrying a basket of onions to sell and resented being kept from the market. Pei remembered him as a wiry young man; he remembered her as the girl who brought bread. Each denied the other's description by standing there older. The onions remained between them during the interview, filling the office with a sharp, ordinary smell.

forest_03_039.speaker: narrator
forest_03_039.text: The road crew leader said the higher stone had marked the rebuilt cart approach, not a new property boundary. He had followed an engineer's pegged line. He remembered a painted arrow on the marker because his youngest child had asked whether it pointed to the moon. The arrow had weathered away. He did not remember who had carried the stone or whether the engineer's written order had mentioned the winter passage. Pei's expectation of a complete answer faded.

forest_03_040.speaker: pei_yun
forest_03_040.text: You used to tell stories as though you remembered every nail in a bridge. I should not have believed that meant you remembered every instruction. I am glad you came. I am also sorry I kept imagining your memory would let me repair mine. Sell your onions. The office will pay the agreed travel and waiting allowance before you leave. If you find the old order, send word. Do not search all night because I look disappointed.

forest_03_041.speaker: narrator
forest_03_041.text: The former leader grumbled that his wife had kept the papers, then paused. He could ask her whether she wanted to look. Pei agreed. At the market he sold half the onions before noon. Lin saw him arguing cheerfully over a bowl's worth with a woman who knew exactly how soft the bottom layer was. His usefulness to their inquiry had not consumed his whole visit. That seemed a better outcome than the perfect witness Pei had hoped to summon.

forest_03_042.speaker: narrator
forest_03_042.text: By evening, the licence office acknowledged the conflicting lines and placed the disputed northern wedge on hold pending comparison with the surviving road order and a second field check. Existing licensed work could continue. The hold would anger those who expected its timber. It would protect the slope from becoming evidence made mostly of stumps. Shi Lan read the notice twice, then took it to the gate herself. Wen followed, wanting to hear how the foreman received it.

forest_03_043.speaker: narrator
forest_03_043.text: The foreman read the hold notice without moving his lips. His crew stood behind him, waiting for a reaction they could use. He said the new marker had guided work for eleven years. Shi Lan agreed that it had guided carts. She asked him to bring the cutting instructions that treated it as a licence boundary. He took the notice inside. Wen remained outside until his uncle came out and asked whether they had any onions left.

forest_03_044.speaker: narrator
forest_03_044.text: At supper, the uncle spoke about onions for so long that his avoidance became almost funny. Wen finally asked whether he had seen northern wood arrive at the kiln. The uncle said yes, before the hold, marked with the foreman's usual blue stroke. The stroke named a crew; it did not prove a permitted stand. He had never asked which line the cutters followed. Wen put down his spoon. His sister told them both to eat before their soup became another investigation.

forest_03_045.speaker: wen_cai
forest_03_045.text: I keep finding places where we did not ask. My uncle did not ask about the stand. I did not ask about the sacks he turned over. The foreman did not ask whether a repayment promise could include land he had not been granted. You keep asking, and I am glad, and sometimes I wish you would stop long enough for us to remember something that is not a mistake. Tomorrow, bring your bowl to our house. My sister makes dreadful bean cakes.

forest_03_046.speaker: narrator
forest_03_046.text: The bean cakes were not dreadful. Wen's sister watched Lin bite one and demanded a truthful judgment. Lin said the middle was excellent and the edge could probably mend a bucket. The sister laughed, then put the hardest cake beside her intended husband's tool kit. He had been working late at the grain house and fell asleep with his boots on. Wen covered the boots with a cloth so they would not stain the newly scrubbed bench.

forest_03_047.speaker: narrator
forest_03_047.text: A message from the lower clinic arrived before morning. The injured kiln worker's breathing remained stable, but he would need another week away from smoke and heavy carrying. The keeper arranged his replacement within the paid crew allotment. Rong's temporary missed-shift payment covered the immediate interval; the employer's accident claim remained open. The worker sent back a request for his old cup. It had a chip his brother hated. The cup was found, washed, and delivered.

forest_03_048.speaker: narrator
forest_03_048.text: On the eleventh morning the assistant, Shi Lan, Wen, and Lin went to the disputed wedge with the foreman. He carried his working sketch in a flat wooden sleeve. The high marker was its starting point. From there, his pencil line followed the shortest accessible ridge instead of the older survey's turn. He said he had drawn it after the road clerk pointed out the route. The road clerk's exact words would now matter.

forest_03_049.speaker: shi_lan
forest_03_049.text: We can walk your line today without accepting it as the boundary. Show us where the first cut happened and where the last one ended. The assistant will compare them against both recorded lines. If the instruction was wrong, we need to know how far the wrong instruction reached. Standing here and telling me you acted sensibly will not show me the stumps. I already understand why the higher road was easier.

forest_03_050.speaker: narrator
forest_03_050.text: The foreman led them to a shallow bowl where young coppice grew among older trunks. Fresh stumps formed an uneven row. Snow filled some cuts; others were sheltered beneath branches. The assistant assigned each a number on his sketch. Wen recognized the foreman's habit of leaving a high notch on sloping ground. The foreman recognized his recognition and looked annoyed. Lin kept her attention on the assistant's measuring pin, letting the two men carry their own strained silence.

forest_03_051.speaker: narrator
forest_03_051.text: One stump had a blue stroke half hidden beneath bark. The foreman said the tree had been marked for his crew before cutting. Shi Lan scraped no wood away; she examined the exposed edge and asked when the marking crew had entered. He gave a date. It preceded the northern application. The assistant wrote it down. A prior mark might identify preparation, or older permitted work, or a mistaken instruction. The missing marking sheet would distinguish those possibilities better than an argument.

forest_03_052.speaker: narrator
forest_03_052.text: At the bowl's lower edge, cut branches had been stacked across the old passage to make a cart loading platform. The foreman called it temporary. It was temporary in the sense that men could dismantle it, not in the sense that animals or elderly gatherers could pass through it now. Shi Lan ordered the platform opened at the walking turn. The crew could retain its usable logs in a safe stack above the route while the question of title remained unsettled.

forest_03_053.speaker: wen_cai
forest_03_053.text: I helped build this. We were told the old track had no users. We carried the branches downhill because it saved dragging them twice. I remember thinking the ground looked worn, and I remember deciding that did not matter because the paper said it was disused. I am saying this before you ask. I would like that to make me feel better. It does not. Give me the saw for the bound crosspiece.

forest_03_054.speaker: narrator
forest_03_054.text: The foreman fetched two additional workers and opened the platform under Shi Lan's direction. They moved the timber to stable ground rather than rolling it into the gully. The work consumed most of the morning. Lin carried smaller branches, following Wen's pace. Her gloves snagged on every fork. She had wanted an inquiry that exposed a decisive lie. Instead, she found herself untangling brush from a mistake she could understand too readily.

forest_03_055.speaker: narrator
forest_03_055.text: Near noon, a sound came from the hollow below them: a short, sharp call, answered by a deeper one. Shi Lan raised her hand. Everyone stopped moving. A smaller Hart stood among the reeds, its pale shoulders visible against the black water. One rear leg moved stiffly. The larger animal waited uphill, partly hidden by branches. Its antlers lowered when a worker reached for his saw. Shi Lan told him to put the saw down slowly.

forest_03_056.speaker: narrator
forest_03_056.text: The smaller Hart tried the newly opened passage and stopped at the remaining crosspiece. Its breathing showed in brief white clouds. The larger animal scraped the ground once. Wen whispered that they only needed to pull one branch away. Shi Lan shook her head. Men approaching the trapped animal might make the larger one charge. They would retreat behind the loading rise, leaving the opening quiet, and see whether the pair could pass without another intervention.

forest_03_057.speaker: lin_yue
forest_03_057.text: I can see the branch from here. That is what makes waiting difficult. I keep imagining the single movement that would remove it, without imagining all the movements the animal might make while I get there. I will come back with you. Wen, leave the tool where Shi Lan points. We can retrieve it later. If the Hart takes an interest in it, you may complain about its borrowing manners from behind the rise.

forest_03_058.speaker: narrator
forest_03_058.text: They withdrew together. The foreman moved last, breathing hard through his nose. From behind the rise they could hear branches crack, then a splashing scramble. A pale back appeared briefly on the upper path. The larger Hart followed, so close that its antlers brushed the smaller one's flank. Nothing about the passage looked graceful. When both disappeared into the trees, Wen sat down in the snow and discovered that he had been holding his breath.

forest_03_059.speaker: shi_lan
forest_03_059.text: We will not follow them today. I want the injured leg described to the district animal keeper and the remaining obstruction removed after the route is quiet. If a snare caused that wound, someone qualified should examine it. If ice caused it, chasing the pair will not improve the leg. Either way, the cabbage owner deserves his barrier and replacement food. He does not have to pay for our desire to call the forest beautiful.

forest_03_060.speaker: narrator
forest_03_060.text: On the cleared route they found a loop of thin iron wire caught beneath a root. The wire had been snapped, its remaining end twisted around a buried stake. It was low enough to catch a leg. Shi Lan kept people off the surrounding snow until the assistant drew its position. She removed it with the stake intact and wrapped the pointed end. The nearby blood might belong to the Hart; the wire itself was certain.

forest_03_061.speaker: narrator
forest_03_061.text: The foreman denied laying the wire. Wen believed him, then wondered whether belief had become easier because he wanted one thing the man had not done. Shi Lan asked each worker where he had seen traps, if anywhere, and said anyone who removed another should preserve its location rather than pocket it. The district keeper would decide what kind of snare it was. The cutting crew's mistakes did not excuse making it responsible for every harm in the hollow.

forest_03_062.speaker: narrator
forest_03_062.text: By the time they reached the village, snow had begun again. Pei met them at the gate with the renewed commission notice. The next fortnight's wages and essential expenses had been approved after the scheduled review; proposed additional work still required its own authorization. She looked at the wrapped stake and knew the field day had changed the plan. Lin looked at Pei's dry sleeves and envied them until she noticed the ink rubbed into her cuffs.

forest_03_063.speaker: narrator
forest_03_063.text: In the lodging room, Wen laid his soaked gloves beside the stove and stared at them. Lin hung hers farther from the heat. He said the foreman had helped clear the passage without demanding payment first. She said she had seen that. He said it did not make the advance clause harmless. She said she had seen that too. They sat with both observations until the niece entered, demanding help repairing the paper Hart's fallen antler.

forest_03_064.speaker: narrator
forest_03_064.text: The district animal keeper sent a written reply the following morning. Frostroot Harts used several high-to-low routes during hard freezes; this hollow was one recorded winter refuge, not the species' entire range. Recent reports from neighboring valleys showed fewer young animals than the last winter count. That did not tell the keeper what had injured the small Hart here. A field assistant would come when the upper road permitted, with ordinary examination tools and experience of approaching frightened bodies.

forest_03_065.speaker: shi_lan
forest_03_065.text: Until then, the narrow passage stays free of traps and gathering parties use the wider bend during daylight. Families can still reach their wood lots. I will post a walking watch for the first two mornings while people learn the turn. The watch does not hunt the Harts. If the animals enter the houses, it warns people to shelter and calls the qualified crew. Nobody wins a medal for trying to demonstrate courage with a cabbage knife.

forest_03_066.speaker: narrator
forest_03_066.text: The cabbage farmer heard the rule and asked whether his fourteen replacements had been forgotten among all the exciting tracks. They had not. The storehouse delivered twelve sound cabbages and two equivalent portions of preserved greens, after he agreed that the mixed replacement suited his kitchen. He rejected one soft head before signing. Shi Lan seemed pleased. A man allowed to inspect his compensation had less reason to believe the warden's concern ended at the forest edge.

forest_03_067.speaker: narrator
forest_03_067.text: Long Qian watched the delivery from the grain-house steps. His own stock of preserved greens was being held against a contract that now looked uncertain. He asked the clerk how much relief food remained. The clerk answered within the public allocation totals. Long wrote something in his book, then went inside. Lin wondered whether he was preparing another purchase or another objection. She no longer mistook the neatness of his writing for the neatness of his intentions.

forest_03_068.speaker: narrator
forest_03_068.text: The old road order arrived with the former crew leader's wife, who had found it beneath winter bedding rather than among her husband's papers. She sold dried pears at the market while Pei read it. The order authorized rebuilding the cart approach above the flood damage. It expressly retained existing land titles and winter passage arrangements pending a later land survey. No later survey was attached. Pei read the last sentence twice, more slowly the second time.

forest_03_069.speaker: pei_yun
forest_03_069.text: The engineer knew exactly which distinction mattered. We lost it by using the visible road stone for too many purposes. I am relieved to see the sentence. I am also ashamed that it took a household cupboard to return it to this office. Keep the original with its owner unless she agrees to deposit it. We need a certified copy and her account of where it has been, not another convenient disappearance.

forest_03_070.speaker: narrator
forest_03_070.text: The owner permitted the land office to copy the order while she retained her original. Her late husband had been the engineer's assistant, she explained; he had kept his own duplicates after retiring. The office recorded that provenance and checked the seal against another surviving road instruction. Lin helped weigh the corners while the clerk copied. Pei did not reach for the page. She had begun the week certain that every relevant paper ought to be in her drawers.

forest_03_071.speaker: narrator
forest_03_071.text: The copy settled the purpose of the higher stone more securely than anyone's memory could. It did not redraw every present property line. The land office would use the old survey, surviving physical points, and a second measured comparison before certifying the disputed segment. Meanwhile, the higher marker could continue guiding carts. Wen looked relieved that a stone could be wrong for one task and still useful for another. He said his uncle might appreciate that principle.

forest_03_072.speaker: narrator
forest_03_072.text: At the kiln, the marking sheet was finally found rolled inside a tool cupboard. It listed the disputed trees as prospective northern stock, with a small notation beside the total: permission pending. The foreman had read the total, then assigned cutters from his working sketch. Rong's clerk had asked for an expected yield from the marked stand. Neither instruction made the pending permission disappear. The physical cuts had happened before the commission arrived.

forest_03_073.speaker: rong_sui
forest_03_073.text: My clerk wanted a quantity to put in the proposal. The foreman wanted a quantity he could promise against the advance. Between them, a conditional plan became work already done. I will carry both instructions to my employer. I will also pay for the marked logs to be kept separate while the land office decides their disposition. I do not own disputed timber because I paid for the hope of receiving charcoal from it.

forest_03_074.speaker: narrator
forest_03_074.text: The foreman said separation would cost labor and spoil his remaining schedule. Rong asked what he proposed instead. There was no answer that did not include quietly using the logs. Shi Lan authorized paid handling from the investigation's approved evidence expense, with the commercial parties' possible reimbursement reserved for later decision. Lin disliked the need to spend communal funds preserving a commercial mistake. The alternative was to let the mistake become fuel and then argue over ashes.

forest_03_075.speaker: narrator
forest_03_075.text: At home, Wen's sister asked whether the disputed wood might have supplied their roof. He said some longer pieces could have, if it had been lawfully available. Her intended husband ran his palm over the unfinished frame and said they would use the lighter timber after all. The revised spacing required another day's work. They arranged that day with the carpenter and accepted the quoted cost. Wen offered his next free afternoon, and she accepted without pretending it was effortless.

forest_03_076.speaker: wen_cai
forest_03_076.text: I wanted the forest to owe us something. We work in it, freeze in it, carry its weight, and still cannot buy four good beams. That feeling does not tell me which four beams are ours. I hate admitting that. My sister was quicker about it. She said the roof only needs to stop rain, not defeat every unfair thing that has happened to the family. I have been trying to build a much larger roof in my head.

forest_03_077.speaker: narrator
forest_03_077.text: The niece's mother returned for her scheduled visiting day with flour on one sleeve and a tired smile that brightened when the child ran to her. Shi Lan stepped aside. The girl had saved every paper animal, including two that no longer stood. Her mother admired them all. Lin watched the warden count the child's mittens after they embraced, then stop herself and ask whether she would like tea. Care could look like fussing when there was no danger left to manage.

forest_03_078.speaker: shi_lan
forest_03_078.text: My sister says I speak to the girl as though she is a small weather emergency. I used to deny it. Last winter I asked whether she had eaten six times in one afternoon. The seventh time, she held up an empty bowl and said, 'You may inspect the evidence.' Wen taught her that phrase. I have considered banning him from the kitchen. Unfortunately, he repairs her paper creatures better than I do.

forest_03_079.speaker: narrator
forest_03_079.text: During the visit, Lin took the afternoon messenger turn so Shi Lan could stay indoors. The work was ordinary and wet. She carried the corrected road description to the gate, the kiln, and the gathering shelter, where people asked different practical questions about it. By the final stop, she was hoarse. A woman gave her warm pear water and said she had explained enough; the posted map would answer the next person. Lin drank with gratitude bordering on surrender.

forest_03_080.speaker: narrator
forest_03_080.text: At the gathering shelter, a charcoal dealer from another district had left a notice offering premium payment for uncommon antler scrap and winter hides. It named licensed trading requirements in small print. The notice did not admit trapping, nor did it prove that the dealer had set the wire. Its timing worried the local watch. Shi Lan asked that the district animal keeper examine it alongside the snare, rather than let a rumor attach itself to the nearest profitable name.

forest_03_081.speaker: narrator
forest_03_081.text: The two buyers submitted their customer terms that evening. Rong's eastern heating orders permitted equivalent seasoned firewood for a minority of customers but charged him carriage beyond the town gate. Long's grain-house agreements permitted mixed suitable fuel if kitchen temperatures and meal service were maintained. Neither could simply replace every requested bag with any wood at hand. Both had more flexibility than their first speeches suggested. The coming allocation meeting would now have something firmer to discuss.

forest_03_082.speaker: long_qian
forest_03_082.text: I spoke as though the charcoal number and the meal number were the same. They are related; they are not identical. Repairing the stove doors has changed the daily use. Some kitchens can take split dry wood. I still need a reliable plan before I reduce the order. If Rong can show that his customers can change too, we may be arguing over a smaller shortage than we feared. I would enjoy discovering that without being congratulated for it.

forest_03_083.speaker: narrator
forest_03_083.text: Pei arranged two inquiries for the next morning. One would compare the buyers' working correspondence with the licence applications and grain advances. The other would follow the upper cutting trail to the remaining marked stand, checking the uncompleted work and the winter road. Each had qualified people assigned, regardless of Lin's choice of accompanying role. She could not walk both routes in one day. She could decide which discomfort she wanted to understand from close enough to ask about it.

forest_03_084.speaker: narrator
forest_03_084.text: That night the valley was quieter than it had been since Lin arrived. The injured worker slept in his brother's room. Wen's uncle rested his thumb. The higher stone waited on its road, uselessly accused of things people had done around it. In the hollow, two pale bodies moved beyond the lanterns. Lin folded tomorrow's route notes beside her cup and listened to Shi Lan's niece telling her mother a story in which the Hart got all fourteen cabbages back.
